   South Gate Parks & Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting Minutes
  April 11, 2024

CALL TO ORDER - Chair Flores called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m.

FLAG SALUTE - by Commissioner Pelayo

ROLL CALL - by Ana Medina, Sr. Secretary
Present: Chair Alan Flores, Vic Chair Lizette Ruiz, and Commissioner Edgar Pelayo. Secretary Jennifer
Cypert has resigned as a Parks & Recreation Commissioner.
Staff: Director Steve Costley, Parks Superintendent Glenn Massey, and Recreation Supervisor Donna (Nicki)
Salazar.

APPROVAL OF MEETING MINUTES
Recommended Motion: Motion to approve the minutes as presented
02/08/24 Minutes M/S/C: Commissioner Pelayo/Chair Flores to approve the minutes as presented
11/09/23 Minutes M/S/C: Vice Chair Ruiz/Commissioner Pelayo to approve the minutes as
presented
12/14/23 Minutes M/S/C: Commissioner Pelayo/Vice Chair Ruiz to approve the minutes as
presented

PUBLIC COMMENTS - None

OPEN SESSION ITEMS

1. ELECTIONS AND REORGANIZATION
Recommended Motion: Commissioners to nominate and approve a Chair, Vice Chair, and Secretary for
the coming year. M/S/C: Commissioner Pelayo/Vice Chair Ruiz to keep the board as is with Commissioner
Pelayo as Secretary.
Director Costley reviewed this item; a discussion ensued.

2. ANNUAL PARKS FACILITY MAINTENANCE REPORT
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file.
M/S/C: Vice Chair Ruiz/Secretary Pelayo
Parks Supt. Massey reviewed this item; a discussion ensued. Secretary Pelayo asked for status on the
fencing project; Director Costley said he would review it at the Director's Repot. Vice Chair Ruiz asked for
the routine to clean after an event, Parks Supt. Massey replied that for picnics staff will leave additional
trash bags for the patrons.

3. ANNUAL REPORTS FROM PARTNER ORGANIZATIONS
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file.
M/S/C: Vice Chair Ruiz/Secretary Pelayo
Director Costley explained this item; a discussion ensued. Vice Chair Ruiz asked if they provide
sponsorships; Director Costley explained that there is the organizations option. Chair Flores asked if the
Friends help; Director Costley replied yes, when asked. Vice Chair Ruiz asked for clarification on what
she's heard on the lack of support for Aztecs Football, Director Costley explained that they are having

  Page 1 of 3
  4
 problems with LAUSD obtaining space for practices and games. Secretary Pelayo asked why are they
allowed to have fields at SG Park then and who handles problems with the Partner Organizations, Director
Costley replied that it is a Council direction to allow them use of the fields and pool; each Organization has
a liaison from Parks Department. He also asked why the reports are different, Director Costley replied the
organizations are asked to report on the achievements of the past year and the goals of the upcoming year
as per the guidelines of Park Policy #9. He will have staff email the Commissioners a copy of the policy.
Chair Flores mentioned that he has been coming to SG Park and participated in most offered sports, Parks
do a great job with the organizations.

4. GROUNDS AND PARKS FACILITY MAINTENANCE 2ND QUARTER REVIEW FY 2023/24
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file.
M/S/C: Secretary Pelayo/Vice Chair Ruiz
Parks Supt. Massey went over this item; a discussion ensued. Vice Chair Ruiz stated that staff is doing a
great job. Secretary Pelayo mentioned the gopher problem at Hollydale Regional Park, Parks Supt. Massey
explained that Grounds Senior Worker Hernandez is doing a great job of eradicating them. He has been
trapping between 30 to 60 gophers per day.

5. RECREATION PROGRAMING 2ND QUARTER REVIEW FY 2023/24
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file.
M/S/C: Vice Chair Ruiz/Secretary Pelayo
Recreation Supv. Salazar reviewed this item and highlighted the special events; a discussion ensued, the
Commissioners commended staff for doing such a great job on the special events.

6. ANNUAL PROGAM FEE RECOMMENDATIONSATIONS
Recommended Motion: Motion to approve the proposed program fee schedule for May 12, 2024 to May
11, 2025.
M/S/C: Secretary Pelayo/Vice Chair Ruiz
Director Costley explained this item; a discussion ensued. Vice Chair Ruiz asked how our fees compare
with other cities; Director Costley said that they are comparable.

DIRECTOR'S REPORT / CALENDAR OF EVENTS
Director Costley: The fencing project is almost completed. The resurfacing of the North Playground was
completed, the JAA Opening Day is May 4, Earth Day is April 20.

Parks Supt. Massey: Diamond renovations are being done after fencing. The irrigation is turned off,
checking them during the day. Twenty azaleas were planted in the Azalea Garden at the Senior Center.
Staff is working on preparing for the summer.

Recreation Supervisor Salazar: These are the upcoming events, Memorial Day on May 25, Concerts in the
Park will be each Friday in July and Movies in the Park each Friday in August. In the Senior Center on
Thursdays there's dancing with a DJ providing the music and new TV's were installed. The Art Gallery is
hosting a new exhibit, Home Town Hero each Saturday until June 1. Biggest Loser contest has culminated.
Adult softball is getting set to begin. Spring Fit 5K will be on May 11. The first glow-in-the-dark pickle ball
event was very successful.

PARKS & RECREATION COMMISSION SUB-COMMITTEE REPORTS
Chair Flores: Nothing additional to report at this time.

Parks & Recreation Commission Minutes of April 11, 2024  Page 2 of 3
  5
 Vice Chair Ruiz: How will staff prevent people from hitting balls against the fence and the status of the
Urban Orchard and Hollydale Community Park; Director Costley said there are signs on the fences to not hit
the balls against the fence, but people ignore them. Work is still stalled on the Urban Orchard by LA
County; the contractor at Hollydale Community Park passed away and it has been difficult to have another
company coming to continue where he left off.

Secretary Pelayo: Can more no smoking signs be put up, Director Costley explained there are signs with
park rules throughout the park and are enforced by both the Park Rangers and Executive Management.
Inquired about touch pads at the pool, Director Costley explained about them. What is being done about
the flooding at Diamond #4, Parks Supt. Massey replied that staff is looking into resolving the issue. Would
like a copy of Parks Policy #9.

REQUEST FOR ITEMS ON FUTURE AGENDAS - None

ADJOURNMENT - At 8:45 p.m. Chair Flores asked for a motion to adjourn.
M/S/C: Secretary Pelayo/Vice Chair Ruiz

Respectfully submitted:

Edgar Pelayo, Secretary

   Parks & Recreation Commission Regular Meeting
  May 9, 2024
  STAFF REPORT ITEM No. 1
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  Steve Costley, Director of Parks & Recreation
Date:  April 26, 2024

Subject:  Review of Recreation Programs 3rd Quarter FY 2023/24

Recommended Motion:  Motion to receive and file.

Report Summary:

Aquatics
The Swim Stadium was closed starting mid-December through the entire month of January for
facility repairs. The pool was completely drained, and contractors came in and performed a
variety of much needed renovations to the pool liner, pool tiles and lane anchors. During the
shutdown, the Aquatics Team deep cleaned the locker-rooms, office areas, storage room, and
general pool deck. A big accomplishment during this time was the Aquatics "Learn How to
Create an Account and Sign Up for Swim Lessons" YouTube video!
Doors reopened in February to much success. After more than a month of being closed, we
welcomed back our daily recreational swimmers and Splash Members with over 2,000 active
memberships. Our partner organization South Gate Aqua Coalition, with almost 100 swimmers,
returned to their normal practice hours and they hosted a USA Swimming meet with 5 local
teams and almost 500 participants plus their families. We hosted a Youth Swim Clinic with the
focus of helping competitive swimmers improve their stroke, endurance, and speed, and had
almost 30 participants.  Lastly, we hosted the South-Central Swim League's winter
championships. This 2-day meet brought in over 6 local teams with almost 1,000 participants
and spectators.
Our Learn-to-Swim program for all ages returned in March. We had nearly 500 group
registrations, 100 private registrations, and almost 100 semi-private swim lesson registrations.
While the majority of registrations were for youth, our registrations for adult swim lessons
increased thanks to our targeted marketing efforts. We held one Lifeguard skills in-service for
staff, and one Adult and Pediatric First Aid/CPR/AED class for community members with 10
registrations. The Swim Stadium also hosted the first two of the South-Central Swim League's
spring league in March, bringing in several local teams and hundreds of participants and their
families.

Fitness
Our membership base stayed consistent at just over 4,000 sold/renewed memberships. Fitness
and Sports Memberships saw 10% and 20% increases respectively, while Sports/Splash saw a
  Page 1 of 5

  7
 slight decrease. This is typical of the winter season, as less members utilize the swimming pool
in the colder months.
Daily Admissions increased slightly, particularly in the Sports tier. This is likely a result of the
Junior Athletic Association’s basketball season concluding and allowing more availability for
open-play basketball. Of the 3,480 daily admissions in the third quarter, 1,831 of them were
Adults who play basketball. Our next closest tier was Teens who paid for basketball court use,
which accounted for 519 daily admissions.
Our Personal Training program saw a slight decrease in packages sold but stayed consistent
with hours of Personal Training conducted. This happens when packages are sold towards the
end of the previous quarter and is not reflective of a decrease in demand. The Private, 12-
session option continues to be our most popular option. Our second most popular was the
Semi-private 16-session option.
Lastly, the Sports Center’s annual Open House took place on Saturday, January 13, from 9am-
1pm. It was an opportunity for the community to come out and experience the Sports Center
and its programming, free of charge. We offered condensed Group Exercise classes, promoted
City events and programs, gave away prizes, and had fun activities for families to enjoy. Our
youth sports partner organization, the Junior Athletic Association, had their basketball league on
display. Patrons were encouraged to watch basketball games and participate in NBA style
halftime contests for the opportunity to win prizes.

Youth Sports
All winter classes for youth fundamental sports were filled to near capacity with some at
maximum levels. Winter registrations are typically lower due to weather and temperature.
During this time, basketball and volleyball tend to be more popular because they are held
indoors. Despite multiple rainouts for our outdoor classes, they were still able to complete all 9
sessions. Registrants were consistent and showed up each week ready to learn and
participate.
The Youth Spring Baseball Camp was held the last of March 25-29. Over 10 kids registered to
learn fundamental baseball skills like hitting, fielding, base running, and sliding. Each camper
received a certificate of completion, shirt, and sack pack.
Youth Sports staff are currently working on the curriculum and drills for our Upcoming Basketball
All-Star Skills Challenge on April 29. This event is open to children ages 7-12 and will test their
ball handling, passing, shooting and agility skills.

Adult Sports
The third quarter began with multiple Fall Adult Softball divisions attempting to conclude their
seasons. Luckily Mother Nature obliged, and six champions were crowned. Champions were
awarded the newly re-designed Championship hoodies while 2nd place winners received
customized insulated South Gate water bottles. A total of 36 teams registered across 6
divisions for Men’s and Coed softball.
Open play volleyball continues to be one of the most popular nights (Tuesday) of the week, this
quarter saw a rise in numbers and ended with a total of over 600 drop-in participants.
Open play pickleball was held every Friday night. The program consistently saw over 20-25
participants drop in to try one of the fastest growing sports. Staff constructed four portable
pickleball courts in the Sports Center gym with perimeter lines, rules, and officials. The drop-in
program was designed to drive interest for our first ever Glow in the Dark Pickleball event that
took place on March 29. Over 80 participants registered for the opportunity to play under the
black lights. The Sports Center was transformed into a glow in the dark pickleball arena with
blacklights, glow in the dark tape, nets, paddles, and balls while listening to up-tempo top hits
music. The event was a huge success and spectacle for all involved!
We are still currently recruiting for our Spring Men’s and Women’s Basketball Leagues.

Partner Organizations (Sports):

  Page 2 of 5

  8
 SG Aztecs pre-season football and cheer practices have commenced at Hollydale Regional
Park. The Aztecs are working hard and looking forward to a successful 24-25 season.
SGJAA Winter Basketball Season has concluded; teams faced off in 5 divisions and concluded
with All-Star games and practices for the top players in their respective divisions. JAA Spring
Baseball & Softball are currently conducting clinics and the Spring Season is set to begin on
“Opening Day” 5/4.
AYSO has begun practices at Hollydale Regional Park. They have increased their number of
players and teams and are preparing for their upcoming 2024 season.

Social Media:
We now have almost 5,000 total followers! Last quarter we had over 10 posts, and 145 stories.
We have reached over 10,000 accounts and engaged with over 500. Our new Recreation
Marketing Coordinator oversees the Social Media Task Force and all social media outlets.

Senior Center
Our winter season was very active this year as we scheduled and visited multiple sites for our
excursions. January kicked off our winter excursions with 9 scheduled trips (Valley View Casino,
Academy of Motion Pictures Tour, Pechanga Casino, Orange County Museum of Art,
Sourdough Festival, Riverside County Fair & National Date Festival, Pala Casino, Legally
Blonde the Musical, and Medieval Times). Each excursion was a success with all trips being
filled at capacity or near maximum. For the month of February, we teamed up with Alta Med to
offer a special event for our seniors called Healthy Heart. This event was instituted to bring
awareness to eating healthy, exercising, and doing regular checkups. Overall, we had a great
turn out a lot of quality information was distributed to our participating seniors. Our Senior
Center has also teamed up with Los Angeles Mental Health to provide a support group for
seniors. Due to the high demand for mental health resources, this group now meets twice a
week. Keeping in line with our goals for the year of offering monthly socials for our seniors, this
quarter started with our Valentines Day party. The love in the air was felt with the friendships
that have been formed with one other. For the hopeless romantics it was also nice to see the
couples that come together every day, showing us what true love is. We gave out goodies’ bags
for everyone, had a raffle, and a special gift for the couple that was married the longest. Our
team also hosted a St. Patrick’s party. The Craft group provided our seniors with a green clove
pin, and during lunch we distributed green cupcakes for dessert. We wrapped up this quarter
with our Easter party; our seniors enjoyed goodie bags, a small egg hunt, and raffles. Thursdays
continue to be a major hit as the seniors enjoy themselves with an open dance floor and
karaoke.

Contract/Youth Classes:
Winter contract classes began promptly as everyone returned from the holiday break. The
following classes were at max registration: Baby boogie, Baby Mexican Folk (3-4 years old),
Baby Mexican Folk (4-5 years old), Ballet (3-4 years old), Ballet (4-5 years old), Mexican Folk
(6-8 years old), and Tumbling. Classes worked diligently for the 8-week session to memorize
choreography and perform their routines at our culminating dance recitals. To accommodate all
classes, we hosted two recitals on March 5th and 6th at the Henry C. Gonzalez Auditorium. Each
registered participant was given two tickets and had the opportunity to purchase additional
tickets if needed. Each night brought in 500 spectators per show, and you could visibly see the
joy in both the children’s and family’s faces.
Our internal programming for youth stayed consistent as all classes were near the maximum
capacity. All Tiny Two’s and Tot Time winter programs commenced the week of January 8 th. Tot
Time and Tiny Two’s classes continued throughout the month of February and hosted a
Valentines Day event on February 14. Children were able to have their pictures taken to create
a special project for their loved ones. Classes had small parties to celebrate Valentines Day and
  Page 3 of 5

  9
 gave sweet treats to their classmates. For Lil Chefs, our 5-week program, participants showed
up ready to learn new recipes and enjoy the fruits of their labor. During the first day of class,
children were given safety instructions for both classroom and kitchen etiquette. Participants
were exposed to many different foods during their cooking journey; the following recipes were
executed: meatball subs, chicken nuggets (from scratch), Nutella French toast, chicken pot pies,
zucchini pizza bowls and cake pops.

Special Events:
After a busy summer and fall session, our winter season for special events does slow down a
bit. In the month of January, preparation for Easterfest began. Flyers, posters, and postcards
were created, and we began our marketing campaign. Registration opened in early February
and by week three, the event was sold out with a total of 200 registered children. Due to the
high demand, there were 50 additional spots added to allow more children to register. Even with
the 50 additional spots we were once again able to reach the maximum capacity of 250 children
registered. Easterfest took place on Saturday, March 23, 2024. The event was scheduled to
take place at the South Gate Golf Course, however, due to rain, the event was moved into the
South Gate Sports Center. All patrons were notified of the location change, and announcements
were made via the Parks and Recreation/ South Gate social media pages. The event included
multiple stations: jumpers, a toddler soft play area, face painting, ballon twister, arts/ crafts
game booths and a photo area with the Easter Bunny. Children were also able to participate in
egg hunts that accommodated the different age groups to ensure complete safety. The egg
hunts were separated from ages 2-3 years old (one parent was allowed to assist the child during
the egg hunt) 4-5 years old, 6-8 years old, 9 and over. Children were also given the opportunity
to find a golden egg (2 per egg hunt age) and they were given an Easter basket filled with toys,
candy, and other special prizes! Lastly, what is an event without snow cones; we had the Kona
Ice truck parked outside of the Sports Center for any patrons who wanted to purchase sweet
treats. Planning phases for summer were initiated and our team began brainstorming new
ideas and entertainment for our Concerts in the Park and Movies in the Park, so please stay
tuned for what is it come.

Cultural Arts:
In January our cultural arts team produced a reel that really sung true what Home Town Hero
open call was about. It received great reviews from the community and was a great last push for
submission since the deadline was quickly approaching. Our team was excited to complete a
full bundle of zines that were submitted to the time capsule. The zines produced celebrated the
different cultural months and our Centennial Public Art Scavenger Hunt which concluded in
January. We showcased our museum team on social media to highlight the staff’s individual art
practices and reintroduce everyone for the beginning of the year. This has helped build
relatability and connections with our communities and allows our patrons to seek out and ask
more questions if they have any. Our coordinator met with the Music Center’s Staff of Arts
Grown LA project and there are plans in the works for a performance in March.
In the month of February, we provided a selfcare/check in workshop to the Parents Center at
Southeast High School. Our Cultural Arts Coordinator was selected to by Arts for LA to be a part
of their ACTIVATE – Emerging Arts Leader Cohort. ACTIVATE is an advocacy training and
leadership development program. In celebration of Black History Month, we highlighted Black
Creatives on our social media platform, and shared a fun amplified playlist. We also had our
Black History Month – African American Historical Figures Zine available during our Museum
Public Hours for community to come in and pick up. We were in full curation mode with Home
Town Hero – Hèroe Local submissions and collected all loan agreement forms back from artists
that were chosen to display in group exhibit. In preparation for Family Art Night our staff made
artistic rubber stamps to be used at an art station and reused for our Home Town Hero opening
reception. We promoted Family Art Night via flyers, posters, park marquee and social media.
  Page 4 of 5

  10
 Toward the end of February our coordinator was interviewed by CALÓ News for a profile piece
on the South Gate Museum and Art Gallery.

Family Art Night took place on Friday, March 8 from 5pm-8pm in conjunction with the Azalea
Festival 2024. It was a collaboration with the South Gate Art Association and the South Gate
Museum and Art Gallery. There were 9 different art stations run by SGAA members, Kiwanis
Club volunteers and cultural arts staff. At 7pm there was a special performance by Ballet
Folclorico do Brasil. This performance is in partnership with The Music Center's Arts Grown L.A.
About 250 community members came out and enjoyed an evening of art making. The artwork
drops offs, condition reports and hanging for Home Town Hero group exhibit was completed.
Vendors/artists/artisans were finalized for the opening event and our coordinator finalized all the
graphics for flyers, banners, art labels and booklets for the full run of the show. Staff worked on
a historical Hometown Heros inside of the museum section to play with our group exhibit. The
South Gate Senior High Media Arts Lead Teacher reached out in hopes of possibly displaying
artwork of their students in the art gallery. Our team was able to make room to display their
group exhibit in the lobby and that show will run from April 6 – June 1. In celebration of
Women’s History Month, we shared a playlist featuring women identifying artists and highlighted
women creatives on social media.

  STAFF REPORT ITEM No. 2
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  Glenn Massey, Parks Superintendent
Date:  April 26, 2024

Subject:  Review of Grounds & Facility Maintenance 3rd Quarter FY 2023/24

Recommended Motion:  Motion to receive and file.

Report Summary:

Grounds Maintenance
We continue to host monthly food giveaways for the community at two locations, one at
Circle Park and the other at Hollydale Regional Park, which are well attended.

Thirty azaleas were planted inside the Azalea Garden adjacent to the Senior Citizen
Building. Thirty trees were planted by the Tree People organization at South Gate Park.
Some of the varieties planted were, Pine, Camphor, and Ash.

Staff are working on replacing the groundcover adjacent to the south entrance to City
Hall, staff was only able to obtain 20 flats of Gazania flowers which have been planted
and have contacted a local nursery to procure 20 more flats.

The North Playground at South Gate Park was closed for three weeks so the rubber
surface could be repaired. New parts to some of the play equipment that was broken
have also been replaced during this time.

The infield of diamond one at South Gate Park was resod with 6,500 sq. ft. of Hybrid
Bermuda grass. The pitching mound was replaced as well.

Staff continue servicing and beautifying over 190 acres of park land on a daily basis.

Park Facility Maintenance
Parks Facility Maintenance staff set up and hosted a variety of Azalea Festival events,
Earth Day at South Gate Park/Hollydale Regional Park, Easter Egg Hunt in the Golf
Course, Women’s Club Annual Conference, and Time Capsule placement event just to
mention a few.

  Page 1 of 2

  12
 Due to the high use of SG Park, Staff continues to do a third daily inspection and
cleaning, in the late afternoon to our outdoor restrooms.

We have continued the use of Electrostatic Disinfecting Equipment for more coverage in
our cleaning and disinfecting efforts for both indoor and outdoor restroom facilities,
along with a pressure washing program. These disinfecting and cleaning tools will be
used consistently. Set ups for all events require us to disinfect all tables, chairs, door
handles, and A/V equipment.

We are in full operation with classes, as well as private rentals, picnics, sports activities,
and service clubs’ events. We continue to host monthly food giveaways for the
community at two locations, one at Circle Park and one at Hollydale Regional Park.

The Community Service Worker program is ongoing; we are still limiting intake to 15
people maximum per day.

Parks are busy with many events, classes, picnics, and sports activities. We remain
vigilant when addressing the ongoing challenges with restroom cleanliness with a
routine restroom disinfecting program. This includes the use of the C3 Machine to apply
disinfectants and cleaners. Once the product is sprayed, staff scrubs floors, walls, and
fixtures to insure sanitary conditions.

  STAFF REPORT ITEM No. 3
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  Steve Costley, Parks & Recreation Director
Date:  April 15, 2024
Subject:  Review of Concession Agreements

Recommended Motion:  Motion to Receive and File
Report Summary: Each year the commission reviews the Department’s current
concession agreements and provides staff with recommendations, particularly for those
agreements that are currently up for extension or renewal. Typically, agreements are
those that allow a private business, either for profit or non-profit, to conduct business on
Park property or to operate a program on behalf of the City.
On the following page is a list of the concession agreements that are currently active
along with information regarding their expiration dates.

Staff is in the process of renewing the Batting Cage agreement with Sofive that will
extend the operation for an additional 5 years. Usually we only do 3-year extensions for
this contract, but Sofive has asked that we make it 5 years so that they can make some
major upgrades to the facility and have substantial time to pay for them.

We are also working with both our carnival operator and our Farmers Market operator to
either extend their current contracts or go out to bid for a new vendor. Customarily, we
do not get bids from other carnival contractors as they tend to have an agreement
amongst themselves not to bid for areas already taken by the current company. In the
case of the Farmers Market operator, they are the only non-profit or not for profit
farmers market in the area and thus their pricing is usually lower on a general basis
than others.

Overall, we are happy with the current providers and are not recommending any major
changes at this time.
